title: Does the Galaxy Acceleration Scale Track Cosmic Dark Energy? A Non-Circular Cross-Scale a0(z) Test of de Sitter-Unruh Modified Inertia -- the z=0 Tie, the High-z BTFR Forecast, and Why M_bar Calibration (Not Rotator Count) Is Decisive
description: In a de Sitter-Unruh modified-inertia (MI) framework the low-acceleration scale a0 is fixed to the cosmological horizon by a0 = c H_Lambda / Z with Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.78881, giving the pure-dark-energy-density (canonical) footing a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = 9.355e-11 m/s^2 or the total-density (ALT) footing a0 = c H0 / Z = 1.1305e-10 m/s^2, two footings 20.9% apart carried on every number. The framework does NOT rewrite Type Ia supernova standardization and gives NO new distance formula -- its cosmological background is General Relativity. Its distinctive content is that the dark-energy term in the Friedmann equation is not a free fit but the GALAXY acceleration scale: H^2(z) = (8piG/3) rho_m(z) + Z^2 a0^2(z)/c^2, with a0(z) measurable from galaxy dynamics and Z a single posited constant. This ties a galaxy-kinematic quantity to a cosmic-distance quantity through a0(z) = (c/2) sqrt(G rho_DE(z)) (equivalently a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda_eff/32pi) with Lambda_eff = 8piG rho_DE/c^2; the mixed shorthand c^2 sqrt(rho_DE/32pi) with a MASS density is dimensionally inconsistent and is not used), i.e. a0(z)/a0(0) = sqrt(rho_DE(z)/rho_DE0) -- a bridge LCDM structurally lacks. It adds no dark-energy parameter beyond the GR background: the same rho_DE(z) that fits cosmic distances must fit the galaxy a0(z). The equality a0 <-> Lambda at fixed z is a definition and is circular; the NON-circular test is the joint z-tracking of two independent datasets. We report a METHOD + FORECAST NON-DETECTION with a live cosmology-side hint. (i) The z=0 tie holds: Lambda-blind SPARC a0(0) = 1.181e-10 (+/-16%) vs cosmic (c/2) sqrt(G rho_DE0) gives ratio 1.26 (1.44 sigma, Planck H0) or 1.17 (0.95 sigma, SH0ES H0) -- a definitional anchor, not an independent win. (ii) The DESI DR2 w0wa posterior propagated through the framework relation yields a0(z=3)/a0(0) ~ 0.74 (Pantheon+ 0.775, DESY5 0.737, Union3 0.707; a ~2.2 sigma decline), all overlapping the framework 0.60-0.75 band -- a CONSEQUENCE of the framework relation plus the DESI w(z), the same DESI information seen twice, NOT an independent detection, and it dissolves if w -> -1. (iii) On the galaxy side the distinctive 0.60-0.75 decline is neither detected nor excluded: separability S ~ 0.8 sigma. One clean deep-MOND z=3.25 rotator (the Big Wheel) gives a0(3.25)/a0(0) = 1.31 (+0.93/-0.52), consistent with a constant and excluding the ALT-cH0 ~5x RISE at ~2 sigma, but unable to separate the 0.70 decline from flat. The central finding is methodological: in the baryonic Tully-Fisher (BTFR) estimator a0 is algebraically 1:1 degenerate with baryonic mass (Delta log a0 = -Delta log M_bar at fixed V), so the dominant M_bar systematic is COMMON-MODE and does NOT beat down with rotator count -- with a >= 0.08-dex correlated M_bar floor the test never reaches 3 sigma at ANY N. The decisive lever is M_bar calibration to <~0.05 dex common-mode, not the number of galaxies, and the a0-separable observable that breaks the degeneracy is the full rotation-curve / radial-acceleration-relation transition, not the BTFR zero-point. A theory-side caveat: promoting a0 = c H_Lambda / Z (derived for a STATIC de Sitter horizon) to a0(z) = (c/2) sqrt(G rho_DE(z)) for evolving w is an adiabatic / instantaneous-horizon ANSATZ, not a derived result; a null disfavours the ansatz, not the z=0 relation. The value of a0 and the constant Z are POSITED, not derived; the a0 magnitude inherits Z, so only the ratio/tracking is under test. CREDIT: the interpolation nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y) is Milgrom's (Phys. Lett. A 253:273, 1999, Eq. 9); the deep-MOND V^4 = a0 G M_bar anchor is the BTFR (McGaugh 2005/2012; Lelli-McGaugh-Schombert 2016); the framework's distinctive content is the c H_Lambda / Z coefficient and the a0 <-> rho_DE(z) tie under test. Every load-bearing number is produced by a committed, adversarially verified, exit-0 script (galaxy_a0z.py, confront.py, desi_posterior_a0z.py, verify_equation.py).
notes: Referee-graded writeup (draft -> 4-reviewer adversarial panel [physics/honesty/citation/rigor] -> revise). The physics panel corrected a convention conflation in a shorthand a0-rho_DE relation (the mixed form c^2 sqrt(rho_DE/32pi) with an SI mass density is dimensionally wrong; the paper uses a0 = (c/2) sqrt(G rho_DE) [SI] and a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda_eff/32pi) [geometric], both giving 9.355e-11, independently verified in verify_equation.py); flagged that the Big Wheel is a transitional (g ~ 0.3-0.5 a0), not clean deep-MOND, object whose flat estimator is biased HIGH (anti-decline, so the reading is conservative); flagged the a0(z) promotion under evolving w as an adiabatic-horizon ansatz; demoted the intermediate-z points to illustrative-only (invalid a0 readouts, sign-contested). Both a0 footings carried on every number; Milgrom credited (nu-kernel + BTFR anchor); a0's value and Z remain postulates; framed as a method+forecast NON-detection with a live cosmology-side hint; no 'proves/solved/detection' language for the framework.
